messages:
Sam Carter: Heads-up — Acme onprem POC is blocked on observability handoff. Their console shows a ton of requests with no trace IDs and the Splunk forwarder keeps failing with a KMS error. Can we swarm on this? :eyes:

Priya Nair: On it. Which env and what errors are they seeing exactly? Any sample logs or trace IDs we can hand to eng?

Sam Carter: env=acme-uat-vpc, Private deployment. Error snip from forwarder attached by the customer:

[2026-03-20T14:12:03Z ERROR] forwarder: failed to upload s3://acme-logs/2026/03/20/part.gz KMS: AccessDeniedException Key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:999999999:key/abcd1234

Also they say the request tracing on our Console shows requests but trace_id is blank for anything proxied by their forwarder. They suspect our proxy strips X-Request-Id / traceparent.

Diego Ruiz: Quick checklist from runtime side: 1) KMS AccessDenied usually means key policy doesn't include the forwarder role (or encryption context mismatch on PutObject). 2) If proxy is old it might normalize/strip headers (case/underscore bug). 3) For tracing we look for 'traceparent', 'b3', or 'x-request-id' headers — we map those into our trace pipeline.

Sam Carter: They're on forwarder role arn:aws:iam::999999999:role/acme-forwarder and proxy version v1.1.8. I'll ask them to upgrade but wanted fixes we can apply server-side if they cannot immediately. Example header capture they sent (no x-request-id present):

> GET /api/orders HTTP/1.1
> Host: backend.acme.internal
> User-Agent: curl/7.88.1
> x-amzn-trace-id: Root=1-642b...;Sampled=1
> (no X-Request-Id or traceparent)

Marta Chen: I can update KMS/policy with customer's permission once they confirm principal. Also note: proxy v1.1.8 had a header normalization bug — v1.2.0+ preserves hyphenated headers. If they can't upgrade, we can add a rewrite rule on our side to copy x-amzn-trace-id -> X-Request-Id.

Priya Nair: Good call. Diego, can you paste the minimal nginx proxy snippet we can share with their infra team as a workaround?

Diego Ruiz: Sure — example workaround (nginx) they can drop into their proxy config to preserve/mirror headers:

```
proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $http_x_amzn_trace_id;
proxy_set_header X-B3-TraceId $http_x_b3_traceid;
proxy_set_header X-Cloud-Trace-Context $http_x_cloud_trace_context;
```

That forces the common trace headers into the forwarded request. Also suggest adding a fallback header generator if none exist.

Sam Carter: I asked them to upgrade to v1.2.1 and to add the nginx snippet as a short-term fix. They replied they updated KMS key policy to allow the role but now see PutObject failing with: 'AccessDenied: encryption context mismatch'.

Marta Chen: That is commonly because the forwarder uses a different encryption context than the bucket policy expects (or the KMS key is limited by encryptionContext). If the bucket policy enforces aws:RequestTag or specific x-amz-server-side-encryption-context, we need to align them. I can draft a minimal bucket policy change for them.

Priya Nair: Next steps: Sam — get a sample successful HTTP capture after the proxy upgrade and the KMS/bucket policy change. Diego/Marta — can you both stand by for quick review when Sam posts the capture? If still failing we'll escalate to eng-runtime for deeper tracing.

deploy-bot: forwarder-proxy v1.2.1 published to acme-uat-vpc at 2033344618. :white_check_mark:

Sam Carter: Thanks everyone — I'll collect the post-upgrade logs and post here. If they still see missing trace IDs we'll run a live trace with them and attach a short curl + tcpdump.
